examples.solution_text:
Let $u=e^x$, so $e^{2x}=u^2$ and $u>0$.
$\begin{align*}2u^2-9u+4&=0\\(2u-1)(u-4)&=0\\u&=\frac12\text{ or }4\end{align*}$
Both roots are positive. Substitute back.
$\begin{align*}e^x&=\frac12\\x&=-\ln2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}e^x&=4\\x&=\ln4\end{align*}$

(a) Let $u=4^x$. Rewrite the first term:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}16^x\\&=(4^2)^x\\&=(4^x)^2\\&=u^2\end{aligned}$
$\begin{align*}u^2-7u+6&=0\\(u-1)(u-6)&=0\\u&=1\text{ or }6\end{align*}$
Both roots are positive.
$\begin{align*}4^x&=1\\x&=0\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}4^x&=6\\x&=\log_4 6\end{align*}$
(b) Let $u=3^x$. Rewrite the first term:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3^{2x+1}\\&=3(3^x)^2\\&=3u^2\end{aligned}$
$\begin{align*}3u^2-10u+3&=0\\(3u-1)(u-3)&=0\\u&=\frac13\text{ or }3\end{align*}$
Both roots are positive.
$\begin{align*}3^x&=\frac13\\x&=-1\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}3^x&=3\\x&=1\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Solve, giving exact answers.
(a) $(\ln x)^2-\ln x-6=0$
(b) $2(\log_5 x)^2+3\log_5 x-2=0$
examples.solution_text:
(a) Require $x>0$. Let $u=\ln x$.
$\begin{align*}u^2-u-6&=0\\(u-3)(u+2)&=0\\u&=3\text{ or }-2\end{align*}$
A logarithm can be negative, so retain both roots.
$\begin{align*}\ln x&=3\\x&=e^3\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\ln x&=-2\\x&=e^{-2}\end{align*}$
Both values satisfy $x>0$.
(b) Require $x>0$. Let $u=\log_5 x$.
$\begin{align*}2u^2+3u-2&=0\\(2u-1)(u+2)&=0\\u&=\frac12\text{ or }-2\end{align*}$
Substitute back using index form.
$\begin{align*}\log_5 x&=\frac12\\x&=5^{1/2}\\x&=\sqrt5\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\log_5 x&=-2\\x&=5^{-2}\\x&=\frac1{25}\end{align*}$
Both values satisfy $x>0$.

Let $u=e^x$, so $u>0$.
$\begin{align*}u^2-8u+16&=0\\(u-4)^2&=0\\u&=4\end{align*}$
The repeated root gives one value of $x$.
$\begin{align*}e^x&=4\\x&=\ln4\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: The concentration of a medication is modelled by $C(t)=16(e^{-0.5t}-e^{-t})$, where $t\geq0$ is measured in hours and $C$ in $\mu\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$. Find when the concentration is $4\,\mu\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$. Give the time to 2 decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Substitute $C(t)=4$. Let $u=e^{-0.5t}$, so $e^{-t}=u^2$ and $0<u\leq1$.
$\begin{align*}16(u-u^2)&=4\\4u^2-4u+1&=0\\(2u-1)^2&=0\\u&=\frac12\end{align*}$
This root satisfies $0<u\leq1$. Substitute back.
$\begin{align*}e^{-0.5t}&=\frac12\\-0.5t&=\ln\left(\frac12\right)\\t&=2\ln2\\t&\approx1.39\end{align*}$
The concentration is $4\,\mu\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$ after $1.39$ hours.

examples.derivation: With u=e^x>0, 2u²−9u+4=(2u−1)(u−4). The roots 1/2 and 4 give x=−ln 2 and x=ln 4. This follows the supplied exponential-substitution and natural-logarithm back-substitution methods.
6u²+5u−6=(3u−2)(2u+3), giving u=2/3 or −3/2. Since u=e^x>0, reject −3/2; the sole solution is x=ln(2/3). The explicit rejection matches source Q24(d).

(a) For u=4^x, 16^x=u² and u²−7u+6=(u−1)(u−6), so x=0 or log₄6. (b) For u=3^x, 3^(2x+1)=3u² and 3u²−10u+3=(3u−1)(u−3), so x=−1 or 1. Both rewrites use the supplied index laws and quadratic-substitution method.

(a) For u=ln x, u²−u−6=(u−3)(u+2), giving x=e³ or e^(−2). (b) For u=log₅x, 2u²+3u−2=(2u−1)(u+2), giving x=√5 or 1/25. All four answers are positive; negative substituted logarithm values remain valid. Source Q24(c) and the natural-logarithm inverse properties support both parts.
For u=e^x>0, u²−8u+16=(u−4)². The single repeated root u=4 gives exactly one real solution, x=ln 4. This is a perfect-square adaptation of the source's taught quadratic factorisation method.

For t≥0, u=e^(−0.5t) satisfies 0<u≤1 and e^(−t)=u². Setting C=4 gives 16(u−u²)=4, hence (2u−1)²=0 and u=1/2. Back-substitution gives t=2 ln 2≈1.386294 hours, correctly rounded to 1.39 hours. This valid time follows the source concentration-model substitution method.
